correctness.rationale: Radial diagonalization on monomial degrees gives gamma expectations with finite multiplicity. The gamma CLT/delta method yields asymptotic N(0,1/4) root fluctuation; the square-root mesh has vanishing gaps and dense residues modulo P, proving the full H_(1/8) Fredholm interval. Coherent-state Gaussian translates converge to N(0,1/2), yielding the H_(1/4) Berezin cluster interval. Strict positivity of wrapped heat kernels and injective Fourier multipliers proves strict separation for nonconstant g; the offset inequalities follow exactly. A common-Gaussian coupling yields min(H1/4g)-min(H1/8g) <= L*(sqrt(2)-1)/sqrt(2*pi). For triangular periodic tents heat-flow reflection/Dirichlet positivity fixes minima at zero, and dominated convergence as P grows attains the coupling constant as a supremum. Independent numerical two-tone extrema and offset signs and the Gaussian constant matched the formulas. These calculations are not substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: Important prior domination: the complete 2026-11-01 almost-periodic radial Fock theorem already establishes the two exact lower heat edges, their strict gap for nonconstant profiles, and its broad bounded-amplitude universal optimum over a class containing periodic functions. Its spectral lower-edge assertions are covered; full cluster intervals follow by applying it to ±g plus elementary interval arguments. The distinct surviving claim is the natural sharp bound under a Lipschitz constraint, with large-period tent extremizers; the earlier theorem optimizes an L-infinity bound and uses discontinuous sign bumps, not a Lipschitz envelope. That sharp Lipschitz component is not an immediate numerical substitution of the prior 0.332128 constant. All preexisting spectral/Looi/cosine ingredients are credited; originality is limited to the sharp Lipschitz refinement and its realizing family.
residual_risks: Most of the apparent spectral novelty is already covered by the stronger almost-periodic lower-edge result; do not certify those subclaims as new.
A general Gaussian Wasserstein/Lipschitz heat minimization inequality may independently contain this sharp tent constant under different terminology.
Sharpness is only across varying periods P and is not attained for fixed nonconstant periodic profile.

The broader spectral classification is valuable context but is not treated as independently novel.
